name: Steve Albini
hook: A recording engineer who refused to be called a producer, refused royalties, and recorded Pixies and Nirvana to sound like a band in a room.
blurb: Steve Albini was born in Pasadena in 1962. In 1981, at Northwestern University, he formed the Chicago band Big Black, which used a Roland TR-606 drum machine instead of a drummer, the first documented record with a TR-606 this map has found; they split in 1987. He became famous for recording other bands. He called himself a recording engineer, not a producer, charged a flat fee and refused royalties: he turned down about $500,000 in royalties on Nirvana's 'In Utero' (1993) for a flat $100,000, and his daily rate when he died was $900. His method was to capture the sound of the room with careful microphone placement. He recorded Pixies' 'Surfer Rosa' in 1988 and 'In Utero' in 1993, and founded the Electrical Audio studio in Chicago in 1995. He died in 2024.
